newsitem.title: CHINA: China to help demobilised soldiers find new jobs.
newsitem.headline: China to help demobilised soldiers find new jobs.

text.p: China is expected to demobilise thousands of soldiers during the winter and help them find jobs in the government, the Communist Party or state enterprises, major newspapers said on Thursday.

The State Council, or cabinet, and the Communist Party's Central Military Commission had issued a joint circular recently ordering governments at all levels to emphasise relocation of demobilised soldiers and ensure the work goes smoothly, the Liberation Army Daily and the People's Daily said.
"Arranging jobs for demobilised soldiers is...important to social stability and is a long-term political mission," said the joint circular.

Tens of thousands of soldiers are discharged each year, and the government has assumed responsibility for relocating them as well as encouraging them to learn new skills that would help them in their new jobs.
The circular bans the government, the party and state enterprises from turning away retired servicemen, the newspapers said, adding that officials who reject demobilised soliders would be punished.
The government apparently fears that leaving discharged officers to fend for themselves would affect morale in the People's Liberation Army and could cause social unrest.

"We should strengthen ideological education of demobilised soliders...make them understand and sympathise with the state's difficulties, take the interests of the whole situation into account and accept arrangements for them," the circular said.
